normalizedStatement: If W is a subspace of \real^m having an orthogonal basis \wvec_1,\wvec_2,\ldots, \wvec_n and \bvec is a vector in \real^m , then the orthogonal projection of \bvec onto W is \bhat= \frac{\bvec\cdot\wvec_1}{\wvec_1\cdot\wvec_1}~\wvec_1 + \frac{\bvec\cdot\wvec_2}{\wvec_2\cdot\wvec_2}~\wvec_2 + \cdots + \frac{\bvec\cdot\wvec_n}{\wvec_n\cdot\wvec_n}~\wvec_n\text{.}

title: Proposition at section6-3.xml:1275
normalizedStatement: If \uvec_1,\uvec_2,\ldots,\uvec_n is an orthonormal basis for a subspace W of \real^m , then the matrix transformation that projects vectors in \real^m orthogonally onto W is represented by the matrix P=QQ^T where Q = \begin{bmatrix} \uvec_1 \amp \uvec_2 \amp \ldots \amp \uvec_n \\ \end{bmatrix}\text{.}

title: Proposition at section6-3.xml:1681
normalizedStatement: If W is a subspace of \real^n with orthogonal complement W^\perp , then any n -dimensional vector \bvec can be uniquely written as \bvec = \bhat + \bvec^\perp where \bhat is in W and \bvec^\perp is in W^\perp . The vector \bhat is the orthogonal projection of \bvec onto W and \bvec^\perp is the orthogonal projection of \bvec onto W^\perp .

title: QR factorization
normalizedStatement: If A is an m\times n matrix whose columns are linearly independent, we may write A=QR where Q is an m\times n matrix whose columns form an orthonormal basis for \col(A) and R is an n\times n upper triangular matrix.

title: Proposition at section6-5.xml:617

title: Coefficient of determination

title: Additivity of Variance

title: Definition at section7-2.xml:230

title: Proposition at section7-2.xml:839
normalizedStatement: Suppose that A is a symmetric matrix, that we list its eigenvalues in decreasing order \lambda_1 \geq \lambda_2 \geq \ldots \geq \lambda_m , and that \uvec_1,\uvec_2,\ldots,\uvec_m is a basis of associated eigenvectors. The maximum value of q_A(\uvec) among all unit vectors \uvec is \lambda_1 , which occurs in the direction \uvec_1 . Similarly, the minimum value of q_A(\uvec) is \lambda_m , which occurs in the direction \uvec_m .

title: Principal Axes Theorem

title: Definition at section7-2.xml:1073
normalizedStatement: A symmetric matrix A is called positive definite if its associated quadratic form satisfies q_A(\xvec) \gt 0 for any nonzero vector \xvec . If q_A(\xvec) \geq 0 for all nonzero vectors \xvec , we say that A is positive semidefinite . Likewise, we say that A is negative definite if q_A(\xvec) \lt 0 for all nonzero vectors \xvec . Finally, A is called indefinite if q_A(\xvec) \gt 0 for some \xvec and q_A(\xvec) \lt 0 for others.

title: Proposition at section7-2.xml:1356
normalizedStatement: A symmetric matrix is positive definite if all its eigenvalues are positive. It is positive semidefinite if all its eigenvalues are nonnegative. Likewise, a symmetric matrix is indefinite if some eigenvalues are positive and some are negative.

title: Second Derivative Test
normalizedStatement: The nature of a critical point of a multivariable function is determined by the Hessian H of the function at the critical point. If H has all positive eigenvalues, the critical point is a local minimum. H has all negative eigenvalues, the critical point is a local maximum. H has both positive and negative eigenvalues, the critical point is neither a local maximum nor minimum.

title: The singular value decomposition
